newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Brit Gas seen posting Q3 loss.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Brit Gas seen posting Q3 loss.

text.p: British Gas is expected to report a third quarter loss on Thursday which will be slightly lower than last year.
But analysts say the results will be largely immaterial, adding other things matter more at the embattled utility.
They hope British Gas will give information on the progress of the take-or-pay contracts and maybe set an exact date for the co's demerger.
British Gas wants to split in two some time in the spring, but is trying to bring the break-up in separate transport and trading firms forward.

Analysts said a slight improvement in the TransCo trading arm and less warm summer weather than in 1995 will probably have helped British Gas post slightly better results in the third quarter compared with a year ago.
Estimates for historic net loss vary between 150 and 128 million stg for a traditionally weak third weak quarter after a 181 million stg loss a year ago.
British Gas, which is suffering from increased competition in the gas supply market, is unlikely to comment on recent takeover rumours, analysts said.
Newspaper reported earlier this week that Royal Dutch/Shell Group considered a bid, but the oil giant is now widely believed to have lost interest.

Former monopoly British Gas could be an attractive prey for a company aiming to boost its presence in the UK gas supply market. Its database with names and adresses of all of Britain's 19 million gas consumers could be a valuable asset eyed by rivals, analysts said.
British Gas never discussed the takeover rumours, which have been around in some form or other ever since the company announced its demerger in February.
There is probably a bigger chance that the firm will take the third quarter result announcement as an opportunity to comment on the take-or-pay contract talks, which started early this year.
The contracts oblige the firm to buy gas from North Sea gas producers even if it cannot sell it on.
British Gas earlier said it hoped to be able to conclude several small successful contract renegotiations later this year.
"We would like to hear more on the progress on the take-or-pay contracts and maybe get an exact date for the demerger," said analyst Irene Himona at SocGen.
